properties.name: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park
properties.title: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park
properties.history: Preserves the symbolic birth cabin site and Sinking Spring farm where Abraham Lincoln was born in 1809. The Memorial Building and Knob Creek unit interpret his early Kentucky years. National Historical Park and a cornerstone of Kentucky’s national story.
properties.description: Preserves the symbolic birth cabin site and Sinking Spring farm where Abraham Lincoln was born in 1809. The Memorial Building and Knob Creek unit interpret his early Kentucky years. National Historical Park and a cornerstone of Kentucky’s national story.

properties.name: Camp Nelson National Monument
properties.title: Camp Nelson National Monument
properties.address: 6614 Old Danville Loop 2 Rd, Nicholasville, KY 40356
properties.history: Union supply depot that became a major U.S. Colored Troops recruitment center and refugee camp for freedom-seeking families during the Civil War. National Monument and NHL archaeological district with visitor center interpretation. One of Kentucky’s most important Civil War freedom stories.
properties.description: Union supply depot that became a major U.S. Colored Troops recruitment center and refugee camp for freedom-seeking families during the Civil War. National Monument and NHL archaeological district with visitor center interpretation. One of Kentucky’s most important Civil War freedom stories.

properties.name: Perryville Battlefield
properties.title: Perryville Battlefield
properties.history: Site of Kentucky’s largest Civil War battle (October 8, 1862), with roughly 7,600 casualties as Bragg’s Confederate invasion peaked then withdrew. National Historic Landmark landscape with museum, trails, and monument row. Anchors Boyle County’s Civil War tourism.
properties.description: Site of Kentucky’s largest Civil War battle (October 8, 1862), with roughly 7,600 casualties as Bragg’s Confederate invasion peaked then withdrew. National Historic Landmark landscape with museum, trails, and monument row. Anchors Boyle County’s Civil War tourism.

properties.name: Big Bone Lick Site
properties.title: Big Bone Lick Site
properties.history: World-famous Ice Age fossil beds that drew Jefferson-era scientists and shaped early American paleontology. Designated a National Historic Landmark in 2024 for its archaeological significance. The state park museum interprets megafauna finds and salt-lick history.
properties.description: World-famous Ice Age fossil beds that drew Jefferson-era scientists and shaped early American paleontology. Designated a National Historic Landmark in 2024 for its archaeological significance. The state park museum interprets megafauna finds and salt-lick history.

properties.name: Ashland, The Henry Clay Estate
properties.title: Ashland, The Henry Clay Estate
properties.history: Home and estate of statesman Henry Clay, the “Great Compromiser,” who shaped antebellum politics from this Lexington mansion. National Historic Landmark house museum with gardens and outbuildings. Interprets slavery, politics, and Bluegrass plantation life.
properties.description: Home and estate of statesman Henry Clay, the “Great Compromiser,” who shaped antebellum politics from this Lexington mansion. National Historic Landmark house museum with gardens and outbuildings. Interprets slavery, politics, and Bluegrass plantation life.

properties.name: Historic Locust Grove
properties.title: Historic Locust Grove
properties.history: 1780s Georgian plantation associated with the Croghan family and George Rogers Clark after his Revolutionary campaigns. National Historic Landmark house museum interpreting frontier Louisville, slavery, and early republic life. Public grounds and programs year-round.
properties.description: 1780s Georgian plantation associated with the Croghan family and George Rogers Clark after his Revolutionary campaigns. National Historic Landmark house museum interpreting frontier Louisville, slavery, and early republic life. Public grounds and programs year-round.

properties.name: Liberty Hall
properties.title: Liberty Hall
properties.history: Federal-period home associated with Senator John Brown and early Kentucky political society in the capital. National Historic Landmark interpreted with the Orlando Brown House as Liberty Hall Historic Site. Anchors Frankfort’s riverside historic core.
properties.description: Federal-period home associated with Senator John Brown and early Kentucky political society in the capital. National Historic Landmark interpreted with the Orlando Brown House as Liberty Hall Historic Site. Anchors Frankfort’s riverside historic core.

properties.name: Old State House (Old State Capitol)
properties.title: Old State House (Old State Capitol)
properties.history: Gideon Shryock’s Greek Revival capitol (completed 1830) served as Kentucky’s seat of government until 1910. National Historic Landmark now interpreted by the Kentucky Historical Society. Public grounds and interiors tell antebellum politics and Civil War-era Frankfort.
properties.description: Gideon Shryock’s Greek Revival capitol (completed 1830) served as Kentucky’s seat of government until 1910. National Historic Landmark now interpreted by the Kentucky Historical Society. Public grounds and interiors tell antebellum politics and Civil War-era Frankfort.

properties.name: Dr. Ephraim McDowell House
properties.title: Dr. Ephraim McDowell House
properties.history: House where Dr. Ephraim McDowell performed the first successful ovariotomy in 1809, a landmark in surgical history. National Historic Landmark museum in downtown Danville. Interprets early American medicine and Boyle County’s intellectual heritage.
properties.description: House where Dr. Ephraim McDowell performed the first successful ovariotomy in 1809, a landmark in surgical history. National Historic Landmark museum in downtown Danville. Interprets early American medicine and Boyle County’s intellectual heritage.

properties.name: Whitney M. Young Birthplace and Boyhood Home
properties.title: Whitney M. Young Birthplace and Boyhood Home
properties.address: US 60 / Whitney Young Birthplace area, Simpsonville, KY 40067
properties.history: Birthplace and boyhood home of civil rights leader Whitney M. Young Jr., longtime executive director of the National Urban League. National Historic Landmark in Shelby County near Simpsonville. Interprets education, leadership, and twentieth-century civil rights roots in Kentucky.
properties.description: Birthplace and boyhood home of civil rights leader Whitney M. Young Jr., longtime executive director of the National Urban League. National Historic Landmark in Shelby County near Simpsonville. Interprets education, leadership, and twentieth-century civil rights roots in Kentucky.

properties.name: Churchill Downs
properties.title: Churchill Downs
properties.history: Home of the Kentucky Derby since 1875 and an iconic American Thoroughbred racetrack. National Historic Landmark twin spires skyline defines Louisville’s racing heritage. Pair with the adjacent Kentucky Derby Museum for visitor interpretation.
properties.description: Home of the Kentucky Derby since 1875 and an iconic American Thoroughbred racetrack. National Historic Landmark twin spires skyline defines Louisville’s racing heritage. Pair with the adjacent Kentucky Derby Museum for visitor interpretation.

properties.name: George T. Stagg Distillery (Buffalo Trace)
properties.title: George T. Stagg Distillery (Buffalo Trace)
properties.history: Historic Frankfort distillery complex continuous through Prohibition under various names, now Buffalo Trace. National Historic Landmark industrial landscape along the Kentucky River. Tours interpret whiskey making and two centuries of whiskey heritage.
properties.description: Historic Frankfort distillery complex continuous through Prohibition under various names, now Buffalo Trace. National Historic Landmark industrial landscape along the Kentucky River. Tours interpret whiskey making and two centuries of whiskey heritage.

properties.name: Labrot & Graham's Old Oscar Pepper Distillery (Woodford Reserve)
properties.title: Labrot & Graham's Old Oscar Pepper Distillery (Woodford Reserve)
properties.history: Stone stillhouses on Glenn’s Creek where Elijah Pepper and later Labrot & Graham made whiskey; now Woodford Reserve. National Historic Landmark distillery campus. Interprets nineteenth-century bourbon craft and the Pepper–Crow lineage.
properties.description: Stone stillhouses on Glenn’s Creek where Elijah Pepper and later Labrot & Graham made whiskey; now Woodford Reserve. National Historic Landmark distillery campus. Interprets nineteenth-century bourbon craft and the Pepper–Crow lineage.

properties.name: Burks' Distillery (Maker's Mark)
properties.title: Burks' Distillery (Maker's Mark)
properties.history: Quaint Loretto distillery where Bill Samuels Sr. launched Maker’s Mark, preserving Burks’ Distillery fabric. National Historic Landmark campus with red-wax dipping and visitor center. Anchors Marion County’s bourbon tourism.
properties.description: Quaint Loretto distillery where Bill Samuels Sr. launched Maker’s Mark, preserving Burks’ Distillery fabric. National Historic Landmark campus with red-wax dipping and visitor center. Anchors Marion County’s bourbon tourism.

properties.name: Fort Boonesborough Site
properties.title: Fort Boonesborough Site
properties.history: Site of Daniel Boone’s 1775 Transylvania settlement and the long 1778 Shawnee/British-allied siege. National Historic Landmark archaeological district beside the Kentucky River. Reconstructed fort and museum at Fort Boonesborough State Park interpret frontier Kentucky.
properties.description: Site of Daniel Boone’s 1775 Transylvania settlement and the long 1778 Shawnee/British-allied siege. National Historic Landmark archaeological district beside the Kentucky River. Reconstructed fort and museum at Fort Boonesborough State Park interpret frontier Kentucky.

properties.name: Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill
properties.title: Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill
properties.history: Largest restored Shaker community in America, an NHL historic district of stone and brick buildings. Living-history village interpreting Shaker faith, crafts, and Civil War-era encounters with armies. Major overnight and day-visit destination near Harrodsburg.
properties.description: Largest restored Shaker community in America, an NHL historic district of stone and brick buildings. Living-history village interpreting Shaker faith, crafts, and Civil War-era encounters with armies. Major overnight and day-visit destination near Harrodsburg.

properties.name: John A. Roebling Suspension Bridge
properties.title: John A. Roebling Suspension Bridge
properties.address: Roebling Suspension Bridge, Covington, KY / Cincinnati, OH
properties.history: John A. Roebling’s pioneering Ohio River suspension bridge (opened 1866) linking Covington and Cincinnati. National Historic Landmark engineering landmark and pedestrian/vehicle crossing. Prototype lessons later applied to the Brooklyn Bridge.
properties.description: John A. Roebling’s pioneering Ohio River suspension bridge (opened 1866) linking Covington and Cincinnati. National Historic Landmark engineering landmark and pedestrian/vehicle crossing. Prototype lessons later applied to the Brooklyn Bridge.

properties.name: Belle of Louisville
properties.title: Belle of Louisville
properties.address: 401 W River Rd / 4th Street Wharf, Louisville, KY 40202
properties.history: Steam-powered excursion boat (built 1914 as Idlewild) and the oldest operating Mississippi-style steamboat. National Historic Landmark vessel when docked at Louisville’s waterfront. Ticketed cruises keep working steamboat culture alive on the Ohio.
properties.description: Steam-powered excursion boat (built 1914 as Idlewild) and the oldest operating Mississippi-style steamboat. National Historic Landmark vessel when docked at Louisville’s waterfront. Ticketed cruises keep working steamboat culture alive on the Ohio.

properties.name: Louisville Water Company Pumping Station (Water Tower)
properties.title: Louisville Water Company Pumping Station (Water Tower)
properties.history: 1860 classical water tower and pumping station that pioneered municipal water treatment recognition in Louisville. National Historic Landmark industrial architecture on River Road. Public grounds and museum interpretation celebrate clean-water history.
properties.description: 1860 classical water tower and pumping station that pioneered municipal water treatment recognition in Louisville. National Historic Landmark industrial architecture on River Road. Public grounds and museum interpretation celebrate clean-water history.

properties.name: Keeneland Race Course
properties.title: Keeneland Race Course
properties.history: National Historic Landmark Thoroughbred race course and sales pavilion opened in 1936 in the Bluegrass. Known for spring and fall meets and elite yearling auctions. Public race days and tours showcase Kentucky horse culture.
properties.description: National Historic Landmark Thoroughbred race course and sales pavilion opened in 1936 in the Bluegrass. Known for spring and fall meets and elite yearling auctions. Public race days and tours showcase Kentucky horse culture.

properties.name: Old Morrison, Transylvania University
properties.title: Old Morrison, Transylvania University
properties.history: Greek Revival administration building (1833) designed by Gideon Shryock for Transylvania University, the oldest college west of the Alleghenies. National Historic Landmark campus landmark. Exterior architecture pin on historic Broadway.
properties.description: Greek Revival administration building (1833) designed by Gideon Shryock for Transylvania University, the oldest college west of the Alleghenies. National Historic Landmark campus landmark. Exterior architecture pin on historic Broadway.

properties.name: Jacobs Hall, Kentucky School for the Deaf
properties.title: Jacobs Hall, Kentucky School for the Deaf
properties.address: Kentucky School for the Deaf campus, Danville, KY 40422
properties.history: Landmark building at the Kentucky School for the Deaf (founded 1823), the first state-supported school of its kind in the United States. National Historic Landmark campus architecture in Danville. Interprets deaf education history; confirm visitor access.
properties.description: Landmark building at the Kentucky School for the Deaf (founded 1823), the first state-supported school of its kind in the United States. National Historic Landmark campus architecture in Danville. Interprets deaf education history; confirm visitor access.

properties.name: Daniel C. Beard Boyhood Home
properties.title: Daniel C. Beard Boyhood Home
properties.history: Boyhood home of Daniel Carter Beard, illustrator and a founder of the Boy Scouts of America. National Historic Landmark house in Covington’s riverside historic fabric. Exterior landmark with Scouting heritage interpretation nearby.
properties.description: Boyhood home of Daniel Carter Beard, illustrator and a founder of the Boy Scouts of America. National Historic Landmark house in Covington’s riverside historic fabric. Exterior landmark with Scouting heritage interpretation nearby.

properties.name: United States Marine Hospital
properties.title: United States Marine Hospital
properties.history: Antebellum U.S. Marine Hospital serving inland-waterways boatmen, a rare surviving example of the federal marine hospital system. National Historic Landmark in Louisville’s Portland neighborhood. Exterior architecture and periodic interpretation.
properties.description: Antebellum U.S. Marine Hospital serving inland-waterways boatmen, a rare surviving example of the federal marine hospital system. National Historic Landmark in Louisville’s Portland neighborhood. Exterior architecture and periodic interpretation.

properties.name: Old Bank of Louisville
properties.title: Old Bank of Louisville
properties.history: 1830s Greek Revival bank building by Gideon Shryock (or attributed circle) on Louisville’s Main Street. National Historic Landmark exterior architecture pin on Whiskey Row’s historic corridor. Celebrates early commercial architecture of the Falls City.
properties.description: 1830s Greek Revival bank building by Gideon Shryock (or attributed circle) on Louisville’s Main Street. National Historic Landmark exterior architecture pin on Whiskey Row’s historic corridor. Celebrates early commercial architecture of the Falls City.

properties.name: Mayor Andrew Broaddus (Lifesaving Station)
properties.title: Mayor Andrew Broaddus (Lifesaving Station)
properties.history: Floating lifesaving station vessel associated with Ohio River rescue service, named for a Louisville mayor. National Historic Landmark vessel/station interpreted at the Louisville waterfront. Reminds visitors of river commerce hazards and federal lifesaving work.
properties.description: Floating lifesaving station vessel associated with Ohio River rescue service, named for a Louisville mayor. National Historic Landmark vessel/station interpreted at the Louisville waterfront. Reminds visitors of river commerce hazards and federal lifesaving work.

properties.name: Lincoln Hall, Berea College
properties.title: Lincoln Hall, Berea College
properties.history: Campus landmark at Berea College, founded on interracial education ideals in Appalachian Kentucky. National Historic Landmark building tied to the college’s abolitionist and educational mission. Public campus architecture near Madison County’s eastern edge.
properties.description: Campus landmark at Berea College, founded on interracial education ideals in Appalachian Kentucky. National Historic Landmark building tied to the college’s abolitionist and educational mission. Public campus architecture near Madison County’s eastern edge.

properties.name: Mammoth Cave National Park
properties.title: Mammoth Cave National Park
properties.address: 1 Mammoth Cave Pkwy, Mammoth Cave, KY 42259
properties.history: World’s longest known cave system and a UNESCO World Heritage Site managed as a National Park. Surface trails, cave tours, and Green River scenery make it Kentucky’s premier NPS day trip from the Hardin/Larue corridor. Interprets geology, cave life, and early tourism.
properties.description: World’s longest known cave system and a UNESCO World Heritage Site managed as a National Park. Surface trails, cave tours, and Green River scenery make it Kentucky’s premier NPS day trip from the Hardin/Larue corridor. Interprets geology, cave life, and early tourism.

properties.name: Mill Springs Battlefield National Monument
properties.title: Mill Springs Battlefield National Monument
properties.history: January 19, 1862 Union victory where Confederate Gen. Felix Zollicoffer was killed—an early major Civil War clash in Kentucky. National Monument and NHL with visitor center, driving tour, and Zollicoffer Park trail. Stretch pin south of the Bagdad ring.
properties.description: January 19, 1862 Union victory where Confederate Gen. Felix Zollicoffer was killed—an early major Civil War clash in Kentucky. National Monument and NHL with visitor center, driving tour, and Zollicoffer Park trail. Stretch pin south of the Bagdad ring.

properties.name: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
properties.title: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
properties.history: Mountain pass used by Native peoples and Daniel Boone’s Wilderness Road settlers entering Kentucky. National Historical Park spanning Kentucky, Tennessee, and Virginia with Pinnacle Overlook and Gap Cave. Far southeastern stretch pin for iconic frontier geography.
properties.description: Mountain pass used by Native peoples and Daniel Boone’s Wilderness Road settlers entering Kentucky. National Historical Park spanning Kentucky, Tennessee, and Virginia with Pinnacle Overlook and Gap Cave. Far southeastern stretch pin for iconic frontier geography.

properties.name: Middle Creek Battlefield
properties.title: Middle Creek Battlefield
properties.address: Middle Creek National Battlefield, Prestonsburg, KY 41653
properties.history: National Historic Landmark battlefield of the January 1862 Union victory led by future President James A. Garfield in the Big Sandy valley—eastern Kentucky's premier Civil War NHL.
properties.description: National Historic Landmark battlefield of the January 1862 Union victory led by future President James A. Garfield in the Big Sandy valley—eastern Kentucky's premier Civil War NHL.

properties.name: Pine Mountain Settlement School
properties.title: Pine Mountain Settlement School
properties.history: National Historic Landmark district—Appalachian settlement school that brought urban settlement-house ideals to rural Harlan County education, health, and culture.
properties.description: National Historic Landmark district—Appalachian settlement school that brought urban settlement-house ideals to rural Harlan County education, health, and culture.

properties.name: Wendover (Frontier Nursing Service Headquarters)
properties.title: Wendover (Frontier Nursing Service Headquarters)
properties.history: National Historic Landmark headquarters of Mary Breckinridge's Frontier Nursing Service—the pioneering American effort to professionalize midwifery and rural nurse care in Appalachia.
properties.description: National Historic Landmark headquarters of Mary Breckinridge's Frontier Nursing Service—the pioneering American effort to professionalize midwifery and rural nurse care in Appalachia.

properties.name: Zachary Taylor House
properties.title: Zachary Taylor House
properties.history: National Historic Landmark boyhood home of President Zachary Taylor on Louisville's former Springfield farm. Private residence with limited public access—included for national designation completeness.
properties.description: National Historic Landmark boyhood home of President Zachary Taylor on Louisville's former Springfield farm. Private residence with limited public access—included for national designation completeness.

properties.name: Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area
properties.title: Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area
properties.address: Big South Fork NRRA, Stearns, KY 42647
properties.history: National Park Service river and recreation area protecting the Big South Fork of the Cumberland River across Kentucky and Tennessee—gorges, trails, and historic coal-camp landscapes.
properties.description: National Park Service river and recreation area protecting the Big South Fork of the Cumberland River across Kentucky and Tennessee—gorges, trails, and historic coal-camp landscapes.

properties.name: Fort Heiman (Fort Donelson National Battlefield)
properties.title: Fort Heiman (Fort Donelson National Battlefield)
properties.address: Fort Heiman unit, New Concord, KY 42076
properties.history: Kentucky unit of Fort Donelson National Battlefield interpreting the Confederate fort that guarded the Tennessee River approach—Grant's 1862 western campaign context on the KY side.
